title: transport slice retract
statement:
For a ring sheaf O, an arrow f:V→U, a module sheaf M on C/U and n in N, a retraction of the restriction of M to (C/U)/(V→U) from the rank-n free module transports to a retraction of the further restriction of M on C/V from the rank-n free module.

Precise quantified statement:
theorem transport_slice_retract
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (O : Sheaf J RingCat.{max u v}) (U V : C) (f : V ⟶ U)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (O.over U)) (n : ℕ)
    (h : Nonempty (Retract (M.over (Over.mk f))
      (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin n ↦ unit ((O.over U).over (Over.mk f))))) :
    Nonempty (Retract ((overMap O f).obj M)
      (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin n ↦ unit (O.over V)))

Notions used: [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

proof.text: Push the retraction along the inverse of the iterated-slice equivalence. This functor preserves finite limits through the presheaf forgetful comparison and sends the unit to the unit. Conjugate the mapped retraction by the finite-product comparison and the definitional comparison with overMap. The splitting equation follows by functoriality.
